subject: Operational Lantern — weekly leadership snapshot (wins, risks, asks)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 01 Apr 2029 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: Operational Lantern — weekly leadership snapshot (wins, risks, asks)

Team —

Quick weekly snapshot ahead of QBR prep next week. Keeping this tight so exec time is respected; bolded asks at the bottom.

Wins
- Production latency improvement: Serving runtime patch (v3.8.1) rolled to 60% of Dedicated fleet; median p95 down ~18% on long-tail workloads. Ops validated metric stability over a 72h window.
- Two pilot customers (StellarHealth + Nova Analytics) completed end-to-end validation of regional routing; StellarHealth sandbox passed privacy tests.
- Cost optimization: initial Quant profile for the 13B family reduced token cost ~22% in tests without observable quality drop on our eval set.

Risks / Open items
1) SLA exception request for Peak-3 plan from StellarHealth (see attached SLA_exception_matrix.xlsx). Procurement has flagged the extended retention/kms needs. If we cannot approve a short-term exception, Stellar may request a delayed go-live.
2) Encoder kernel regressions observed in one GPU type after the v3.8.1 rollout; affecting only long sequences (>2k). Engineering has mitigations but requires a brief capacity reallocation next Tuesday to run a hotfix. This will temporarily reduce burst capacity by ~8%.
3) QBR narrative: we still lack a consolidated single-slide ROI example tying latency gains -> user retention for Hosted customers. Analytics needs one more week to finalize cohort attribution.

Asks (actionable — please respond by EOD Wed 4/3)
- Laura: can you sign off on the short-term SLA exception (30d) for StellarHealth if Legal marks the redlines low-risk? I attached the proposed matrix.
- Jonas: can you confirm availability to re-route 2 racks for the Tuesday hotfix window (4/9) and own a 1-hr rollback playbook?
- Kimberly: help prioritize one analyst to finalize the ROI cohort and produce a one-slide artifact for the QBR (need by 4/5).

Attachments: QBR_prep_deck_v2.pdf (PDF, 2.1MB), SLA_exception_matrix.xlsx (XLSX, 120KB)
Drive link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cQBRdeck
HubSpot: https://hubspot.com/deal/SH-4821

Thanks — brief replies welcome.

—
Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Ops 
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Apr 2029 17:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Operational Lantern — weekly leadership snapshot (wins, risks, asks)

Marissa —

Thanks for the concise readout. Two quick items:
1) I'll loop in Legal first thing Tuesday for the SLA exception; if Legal flags nothing material, I can approve a 30-day exception. If there are non-trivial redlines, I will escalate to the COO.
2) For the ROI slide, Kimberly, can you confirm who on analytics can take point? If we can get a one-pager by Friday (4/5) Laura can include it in the QBR deck.

Also, for the hotfix date, Jonas — appreciate an early heads up on the rollback steps; ops should rehearse on staging.

Laura
Laura Bennett
Chief of Staff — Product & GTM
laura@redwood.com

Marissa / team —

I can take the rack reallocation on 4/9. Proposed plan:
- 02:00–03:30 UTC: move 2 racks offline and run hotfix on a canary subset.
- 03:30–04:00 UTC: smoke tests. If green, bring the second rack live and monitor for 2h.
- Rollback playbook: stop rollout, restore kernel version, restart nodes, run smoke tests (I will draft the checklist).

I'll coordinate with OnCall and SRE to confirm the maintenance window on Tuesday morning PT and will share the rollback checklist by EOD Thu (4/4).

Jonas
